agyos_skill.instructions: Your profile is a **conversion landing page, not decoration.** Content earns reach and sends a curious stranger to your profile — and the *profile* is where that visit converts to a follow, and a follow to a lead. Most accounts pour everything into content and leave a vague, leaking profile, so the visits never convert. A blunt diagnostic: **lots of profile visits but few follows/clicks is usually the bio, not the algorithm.** Two commitments: 1. **Clarity beats cleverness.** A visitor decides in seconds. Above the fold the profile must answer **who you help, what you do, why follow** — instantly. A witty-but-vague bio converts worse than a plain, specific one. 2. **Every element has a job.** The name field is *searchable*. The link is the *conversion mechanism*. The banner is *prime real estate*. "Filled in" isn't optimized. > Scope: this skill is **advisory** — it produces a ready-to-apply spec. **WoopSocial publishes posts > and media; it does not edit profile fields**, so the user applies the spec in each app. Load `brand-profile.md`, `social-strategy.md`, `audience.md`, `voice.md`. The profile is positioning made concrete: who you help + the wedge (brand/strategy), the audience's language (audience), the primary goal → the CTA/link (strategy), and the tone (voice). Diagnose the profile as a funnel — **Discovered → Clarity → Follow → Convert** — and find which stage leaks (unfindable / unclear / unconvincing / dead-end). Make sure the above-the-fold answers who/what/why at a glance. Niche down — **"for everyone" converts no one.** See `references/the-profile-funnel.md`. Put a **niche keyword** in the searchable fields — the **Instagram name field**, the **LinkedIn headline**, the **YouTube description** — not just your name or "Founder." Think like your audience: what would they search? Keep the handle searchable and consistent. See `references/element-playbook.md`. Who you help · what you do · **proof** (real only) · **CTA + link prompt** — clarity first, personality second, skimmable, within the limit, on-voice. See `references/element-playbook.md`.
